title: Alpha-thalassaemia
summary: Alpha-thalassaemia affects how the body makes haemoglobin. Most people with a changed copy are healthy; more serious forms happen when several copies are changed.
inheritance_plain: It is more complicated than most recessive conditions because people normally have four copies of the alpha-globin genes. The chances for a child depend on exactly which copies each parent has, so a genetic counsellor works them out from the full report.
carrier_meaning: People with one or two changed copies are usually healthy. Some have mild anaemia that does not need treatment.
disease_meaning: When three or all four copies are changed, the condition is more serious and needs specialist care.
screening: Standard blood tests can miss some carriers, so the result often needs a specialist to interpret it.
